get_source.name: get_source
get_source.description: Read one source by citekey: its summary, findings and notes, or the part `section` names.

heading.description: Only the body under this heading (prefix match)

offset.description: Body slice start (a character offset, e.g. from passages)

passages.name: passages
passages.description: Find a word or quotation in ONE source's full text: the passages around each match (in **bold**), each with its body `offset` (get_source reads on from it) and heading. Literal, case- and accent-insensitive.

citekey.description: The source's citekey (an old, renamed one works too)

query.description: The text to find, matched literally (case- and accent-insensitive); a regex when regex=true

regex.description: Treat query as a Java regular expression (default false)

context.description: Characters of context around each match (default 600, max 3000)

search.name: search
search.description: Search the corpus: sources, compact, with the findings that matched.

query.description: Free text: words AND-ed, "a phrase", -word, or

authors.description: Any one, a substring of an author's name

from.description: Period start, a signed year (BCE negative)

offset.description: The next page's offset, from the listing's footer

facets.name: facets
facets.description: The existing values of one field, with source counts — pick from them instead of inventing new ones.

neighbors.name: neighbors
neighbors.description: A source's typed edges in and out, with each neighbour's status. No edge is NOT evidence of agreement.

kinds.description: Filter to these edge kinds only: references|challenges|refutes|updates|superseded_by

query.name: query
query.description: One read-only SQL SELECT on the corpus database (Postgres) — e.g. every cited source's status at once.

sql.description: One read-only SQL statement (Postgres refuses writes)

get_article.name: get_article
get_article.description: One compiled article by slug: body, summary, the generated coverage sections, the sources it cites (title, year, status), backlinks. `parts` = comma-separated body,summary,coverage,cited,backlinks.

parts.description: Comma-separated parts to return: body,summary,coverage,cited,backlinks (default: all)

followups.name: followups
followups.description: The papers citing a source, each with its citation intents and a proposed edge kind — critiques the article may ignore.

since.description: Only papers published from this year on

limit.description: At most this many citing papers

check_edits.name: check_edits
check_edits.description: Dry-run edits (or a whole draft `body`) against the stored article: which edits apply, and what the review checks find in the result. Nothing is written.

EditAnswer.description: One change to the article body

anchor.description: Text copied EXACTLY from the current body (a sentence, or enough words to occur only once); edits apply in order, so an anchor is looked up in the text the earlier edits produced

text.description: replace: the new text; insertAfter/insertBefore: the text to insert, verbatim (start it with a blank line to add a paragraph); delete: null

edits.description: Edits to the current stored body, applied in order

body.description: Instead of edits: a whole draft body

kind.description: Check the section set of this kind instead of the article's (index = none, for a fragment to be appended)

article_coverage.name: article_coverage
article_coverage.description: An article's recorded filter: its sources, which are cited, each other one's stored reason, the drift (sources with no reason), and the generated Not used list and Method note.

doi.description: The DOI of a candidate, exactly as listed

why.description: Why it belongs to the goal, in one sentence

picks.description: The candidates that belong to the goal, most important first; leave out the rest

severity.description: major | minor — by the severity rules of your instructions

kind.description: The kind your instructions name (e.g. term, opaque, why, lost)

where.description: The section heading, or the first 8 words of the passage

quote.description: The article's words the finding is about, copied exactly

problem.description: What is wrong, in one or two sentences

id.description: The ledger id of your earlier finding (R4, C2, S7…)

fixed.description: true when the current article no longer has the problem

quote.description: The current article's words that show it — the fixed text, or the problem still there — copied exactly; empty only when the passage was deleted

note.description: One sentence: what changed, or why it is not fixed (needed when not fixed)

verdict.description: PASS | MINOR | MAJOR — the worst of your findings

explainBack.description: Five plain sentences: the question, the answer, who disagrees with whom, what is open

emptySlots.description: The slot names you could not fill from the text; [] when all four are filled

lostAt.description: The section where you stopped following; null if you never did

checks.description: One check per earlier finding of yours that the review ledger lists as open (empty when it lists none)
